title: Meteor shower to peak over Belleville tonight with 'ideal' timing and weather
excerpt: Clear skies, a nearly new moon and moderate temperatures are expected to combine to offer prime viewing.
content:
Belleville stargazers will get a chance to see the Draconid meteor shower peak Thursday night, and you won't need to stay up late to catch a glimpse.

While some meteor showers peak overnight, the Draconids' peak will begin earlier. The Draconid meteor shower will peak beginning at 8 p.m. Central Daylight Time Thursday night, according to NASA, and the peak will last into early Friday morning.

In addition to the prime timing, the moon phase and weather are expected to cooperate for ideal viewing conditions.

"This is an ideal meteor shower for casual skywatchers, since it begins soon after darkness falls rather than in the early morning hours," NASA reports. "A nearly new Moon phase means little interference from moonlight, making the shooting stars easier to spot."

The National Weather Service St. Louis office forecasts Belleville will see a low temperature around 58 degrees Fahrenheit Thursday night, with clear skies.

The Draconid meteor shower is named for the constellation Draco, where its radiant is located, according to NASA. Astronomers recommend finding a dark spot, letting your eyes adjust and watching for meteors anywhere in the sky.

The conditions for this year's Draconids are "near perfect," astronomy publication Space.com says. The Draconids can be expected to produce about five to 10 meteors per hour under ideal conditions.

The sun will set over Belleville at 6:31 p.m. Thursday, according to online clock Time and Date.

If you're looking to gather with other stargazers soon, the St. Louis Astronomical Society will host a telescope viewing event 7 to 10 p.m. Saturday, Oct. 17 at Tower Grove Park.

More stargazing events to see from Illinois

There will be three more full moons to catch a glimpse of in 2026, including two "supermoons." Here's when to see them, from Astronomy.com:

  • Monday, Oct. 26: Hunter's moon

  • Tuesday, Nov. 24: Beaver moon (supermoon)

  • Wednesday, Dec. 23: Cold moon (supermoon)

In addition to the upcoming full moons, Illinois stargazers can also enjoy viewing several more meteor showers this year, including the Orionids in October, the Leonids in November, the Geminids in December and more.
